note: Compared with Cook's final ratings and the last public polls. Uncalled races can still shift as more votes are counted.

items.title: Texas flips both top races
items.text: AP projected Talarico (D) over Paxton (R) for Senate, 59.2%–39.2% with about 67% counted, well above final polls (Talarico +3 to +7). AP also projected Hinojosa (D) over Gov. Abbott (R), after a final poll showing a 1-point race.

items.title: Kansas and Ohio Senate flip
items.text: Hamilton (D) unseated Sen. Marshall (R) in a race Cook rated a toss-up. In Ohio, Brown (D) was projected the winner over Sen. Husted (R).

items.title: NY-21 reverses
items.text: Gendebien (D) led early, but with about 70% counted Constantino (R) leads by roughly 6,000 votes, per WWNY 7 News. No call yet.

items.title: Michigan Senate tightening
items.text: El-Sayed (D) leads Rogers (R) 51.1%–47.0% with about 31% counted, versus an 11-point lead in the final NYT/Siena poll. No call yet.

items.title: Republican-held House seats flipping
items.text: Projected Democratic pickups include KY-06, NJ-07, NC-11, PA-07, PA-08, PA-10 and OH-15 (rated Lean Republican). No tracked race has been called for a Republican yet.

items.title: Georgia governor flips after a tied final poll
items.text: Lance Bottoms (D) was projected the winner over Jackson (R). The last InsiderAdvantage poll had the race tied 49–49.
